Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 84, verse 16–25:

﴿So I do not swear by the twilight﴾. Concerning it there are four opinions. The first: it is the twilight of the night, which is the redness, said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: it is the remaining light of the sun, said by Mujahid.

The third: it is what remains of the day, said by ʿIkrimah.

The fourth: it is the day, narrated by Ibn Abi Najih.

﴿And by the night and what it gathers﴾. Concerning it there are four interpretations. The first: "and what it gathers," said by Mujahid. The rajiz (poet) said:

"Indeed we have she-camels, pure-bred, gathered together, or they will find a driver."

The second: "and what it covers and conceals," said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: "and what it drives," because the darkness of the night drives every thing to its refuge, said by ʿIkrimah.

The fourth: "and what it works upon," said by Ibn Jubayr. The poet said:

"And one day you find us righteous, and at another time it raises us up like the one who girds himself for work."

That is, like the one who works.

﴿And by the moon when it becomes full﴾. Concerning it there are three interpretations. The first: "when it becomes complete (istawa)," said by Ibn ʿAbbas; and the saying of them, "the matter became consistent (ittasaqa)" when it became orderly and even.

al-Dahhak said: the night of the fourteenth is the night of al-Sawaʾ (equality).

The second: "and the moon when it becomes round," said by ʿIkrimah.

The third: "when it is joined together (ijtamaʿa)," said by Mujahid. Their meanings are close.

It may also allow a fourth: "when it rises shining."
